newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: UM Land eyes 30 pct profit growth.
newsitem.headline: UM Land eyes 30 pct profit growth.

text.p: Property company United Malayan Land Bhd (UM Land) said on Tuesday it was targeting a 30 percent profit growth for the financial year to July 31, 1997.
UM Land chairman Tunku Shahriman Tunku Sulaiman told a news conference the company also plans to build two new townships in central Selangor state on 14,000 acres of land.
"If they (UM Land management) can show improvement of 30 percent I'm quite happy... That is our target," he said in response to a question on profit growth.
The company on Monday reported a 47.78 percent pretax profit growth to 74.08 million and a 59.47 percent net profit rise to 53.07 million ringgit for the year ended July 31, 1996.
Tunku Shahriman said continued strong growth of the Malaysian economy and an encouraging response to the company's Seri Alam township project in southern Johor state will bolster company earnings.

The two townships under negotiations in Selangor are on 900 acres and 500 acres of land, Tunku Shahriman said. Negotiations are expected to be completed in about a month's time, but he declined to give further details.
UM Land also plans a mixed development in the northern island state of Penang and shophouses in northern Kedah state.
